posts.title: Xiaomi EV delivers 31,267 units in July, 39% of annual target
posts.summary:
Xiaomi EV needs average monthly deliveries of nearly 67,000 units over the remaining 5 months to achieve its full-year target of 550,000 units.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Xiaomi EV delivered 31,267 units in July, bringing its seven-month total to 216,322 vehicles, which accounts for only 39% of its 550,000-unit annual target.
To meet its full-year goal, the company must significantly accelerate production to average nearly 67,000 monthly deliveries for the remainder of the year.

The company is pivoting toward the extended-range electric vehicle (EREV) segment with its new Sky Nomad N90 Max and N70 Max models, which are priced to compete directly with Li Auto and Huawei-backed Aito.
Despite reports of strong pre-orders for the new series, investor sentiment remains cautious regarding the aggressive pricing strategy and the massive delivery gap required to hit annual targets.

posts.title: Chengdu Auto Show opens next week with nearly 120 brands, 1,600 vehicles
posts.summary:
The 2026 Chengdu Auto Show will cover 220,000 square meters, making it China's first A-level show of the second half of the year.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: The 2026 Chengdu Auto Show, China's first A-level event of the second half, will feature 120 brands and 1,600 vehicles across 220,000 square meters.
Major manufacturers are using the event to debut new flagship models, including BYD's D-segment luxury sedan, the Da Han, and Huawei's Maextro V800/V680 MPVs.
The show serves as a critical barometer for southwestern Chinese market demand and a strategic launchpad for automakers ahead of the peak autumn sales season.
Xiaomi will showcase its expanded portfolio by displaying battery electric and extended-range SUV series side-by-side for the first time.

posts.title: Hyundai's first Ioniq model for China to open pre-sales at Chengdu Auto Show
posts.summary:
The Ioniq V is the first production model in China from Hyundai's electric brand Ioniq, and will officially launch in September.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Beijing Hyundai will open pre-sales for the Ioniq V, its first China-produced Ioniq model, at the Chengdu Auto Show with an official launch scheduled for September.
The mid-size electric sedan was developed by Hyundai's China design center and features high-end tech including a Qualcomm Snapdragon 8295 chip and dual AI integration via Baidu and ByteDance.
The vehicle utilizes an 800-volt E-GMP platform and incorporates smart driving solutions from Momenta, supporting L2+ capabilities on urban and highway roads.
Designed for both the domestic market and global export, the Ioniq V offers battery options from CATL with ranges between 520 km and 650 km.

posts.title: Standards-Compliant 112G PHY for Linear Optics: Driving Efficient AI Infrastructure
posts.summary:
112G PHY IP for linear optics to reduce power, latency and thermal load for high-speed data movement in AI and data center systems.
The post Standards-Compliant 112G PHY for Linear Optics: Driving Efficient AI Infrastructure appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Synopsys has introduced the industry's first 112G PHY IP compliant with the OIF-CEI-112G-LINEAR-PAM4 standard, designed to support linear drive optics in high-speed AI infrastructure.
Adopting linear optics can reduce module power consumption by up to 50% by eliminating the need for power-hungry DSPs and retimers within the optical module.
The new PHY IP addresses critical thermal and latency bottlenecks in dense AI racks, providing a scalable path toward 224G/448G speeds and co-packaged optics (CPO).
Measured performance data for the 112G PHY indicates that TX/RX results meet or exceed OIF-CEI specifications, ensuring interoperability within the broader data center ecosystem.

posts.title: Anthropic’s Watermarking, How It (Probably) Works, Worse Than It Seems
posts.summary: Anthropic is adding watermarking in response to the E.U.'s AI law. It's a terrible idea, first and foremost for philosophical reasons.
bullets: Anthropic has introduced watermarking for its AI models primarily to comply with the European Union's AI Act.
The implementation of watermarking faces significant philosophical and technical criticism regarding its efficacy and long-term impact on AI utility.
Regulatory mandates like the E.U. AI Act are forcing AI developers to adopt defensive measures that may undermine the open nature of generative technology.
The move highlights the growing tension between global regulatory compliance and the fundamental design principles of large language models.
